title: Structured output failure injection and canary recovery scenarios
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create an automated failure-injection and canary test harness that validates JSON-mode/enforced-structured-output behavior across streaming, tool/function calls, and constrained-decoding fallbacks. The goal is to catch regressions that only appear under partial streams, interleaved tool calls, or when the runtime activates codec-level backoffs (quantization/kernel fallbacks). The harness will run in CI and in a gated canary environment that mirrors Dedicated traffic patterns.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic failure-injection suite exists that can introduce: truncated streams, sentinel corruption, interleaved toolcall tokens, abrupt kernel fallback events, and artificial jitter on KV cache hits.
Canary pipeline that mirrors 5% of production traffic runs the suite nightly and fails the rollout on SLI degradation (schema-adherence < 99.5% on canonical prompt set).
End-to-end observability: dashboards showing schema-violations by model-version, failure-mode heatmap, and example payloads for first 100 violations.
Automated rollback policy exercised: canary-to-prod rollback triggered and validated in a staged run when regression thresholds are exceeded.

Playbook entries created (runbook link included) for diagnosis steps: reproducer generation, PR triage checklist, and mitigation knobs (strict-decoder fallback, prefix-cache invalidation, token-gating).
implementation_notes: Build a small harness service (pytest-based) that uses recorded production traces to replay streaming events and tool calls into the runtime test endpoint.
Failure modes should be parameterizable: truncate-percent, inject-sentinel, interleave-toolcall-chance, kv-latency-ms, emulate-kernel-fallback.
Use existing schema-checker library (canonicalizer + typed-assertor) to compute schema-adherence and produce structured diagnostics for each failing case.
Integrate with Console: emit structured telemetry events to the schema-violation index and surface example failed payloads in per-model dashboards.
Create a minimal canary job definition (k8s CronJob + GitOps manifest) that runs the suite against canary traffic and wires into rollout gates.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Injecting failure into canaries increases noise; must ensure we don't confuse SRE incident monitors — use dedicated canary metrics namespace.
Replaying production traces requires sanitization of PII; initial rollout will use synthetic traces until DPO signoff is obtained.
Tight schema thresholds can cause frequent false positives for models under active fine-tuning; we'll allow a temporary 'leniency window' and attach regression context.
Complex failure models increase CI time; start with a small core set that covers the most common observed regressions (stream truncation, interleaved toolcalls, sentinel corruption).
comments: 2026-03-03 - Maya Chen: Initial spike finished. Replayed three production traces and reproduced a partial-stream + toolcall interleave that results in malformed JSON 18% of the time. Synthetic traces attached to the design doc.

2026-03-05 - Arjun Patel: Implemented the first harness prototype. It can inject truncated streams and interleave fake tool-call tokens. Observed false positives due to flaky canonicalizer in presence of benign whitespace; added normalization step.
